University Library Research Assistant — PRD v1.0.0 | Team 05 | Squad 69

1. Executive Summary 
University Library Research Assistant is a web-based research assistant designed to help students find concise, 
citation-backed answers from an assigned university library corpus. Instead of manually searching through 
research papers, theses, and course materials, students can ask natural-language questions and receive a short 
answer grounded only in retrieved library documents. 
The system combines document ingestion, cleaning, section-aware chunking, semantic embeddings, vector 
retrieval, relevance thresholding, and constrained LLM generation. Every supported answer must include a 
traceable citation containing the source document and page or section. When the available corpus does not 
support an answer, the system explicitly responds that it does not know rather than guessing. 
This PRD defines the product requirements, user needs, MVP boundaries, evaluation approach, risks, and 
acceptance criteria for Sprint 2. 
2. Business Problem 
2.1 Context 
University libraries contain large collections of research papers, theses, and course materials. Although these 
documents contain the information students need, the information is distributed across many files and sections. 
The current research experience is often: 
●​
Manual — students must open and search many documents. 
●​
Time-consuming — finding the exact supporting passage can take significant effort. 
●​
Fragmented — relevant information may be distributed across multiple documents. 
●​
Difficult to verify — students may find an answer without an immediately traceable source. 
●​
Prone to unsupported answers — general-purpose AI can provide fluent information that is not present in the 
assigned corpus. 
2.2 The Core Gap 
There is a need for a focused intelligence layer over the university's assigned document corpus that connects 
natural-language questions with relevant document passages and produces concise answers with real citations. 
The product must therefore connect:

2.3 Impact 
●​
Students spend less time searching through unrelated documents. 
●​
Answers are easier to verify because supporting sources are shown. 
●​
Research across multiple documents becomes faster and more focused. 
●​
The explicit refusal path reduces the risk of unsupported or hallucinated answers. 
●​
The team gains a clear, explainable RAG pipeline suitable for demonstration and viva.

6. Corpus & Data Source Documentation 
The assigned corpus is expected to contain research papers, theses, and course materials. The corpus must be 
inventoried before implementation so the team understands formats, document length, and extraction quality. 
6.1 Corpus Inventory Requirements 
●​
Count the total number of documents. 
●​
Record formats such as PDF, DOCX, and HTML where applicable. 
University Library Research Assistant — PRD v1.0.0 | Team 05 | Squad 69

●​
Measure or estimate average document length. 
●​
Identify scanned PDFs versus digital-native documents. 
●​
Manually inspect 5–10 representative documents before the ingestion pipeline is finalized. 
●​
6.2 Processing Pipeline 
Stage 
Requirement 
Loading 
Use PyMuPDF / unstructured to extract document 
content. 
Cleaning 
Remove or normalize extraction noise such as 
Chunking 
Use section-aware chunks of approximately 300–500 
tokens with about 15% overlap. 
Embedding 
Use OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, or bge-small-en 
if a local/free alternative is required. 
Indexing 
Store embeddings and chunk metadata in ChromaDB. 
Retrieval 
Embed the student question and retrieve top-k 
semantically relevant chunks across the corpus. 
Generation 
Inject only retrieved content into the LLM prompt and 
require grounded output. 
 
6.3 Data Quality Requirements 
●​
Metadata must be defined before the first full embedding run. 
●​
Page numbers and section information must be preserved whenever available. 
●​
Malformed or unreadable documents must be logged and flagged rather than silently ignored. 
●​
Bibliography/reference sections should be excluded or separately tagged when they create retrieval noise. 
●​
The team must manually validate sample chunks before indexing the full corpus.

10. User Stories 
Epic 1 — Question Answering 
US-101 — As a student researcher, I want to ask a natural-language question, so that I can get a concise answer 
without searching every document. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
A question can be entered in the chat interface. 
●​
The system searches the indexed corpus. 
●​
The response is concise and grounded in retrieved material. 
University Library Research Assistant — PRD v1.0.0 | Team 05 | Squad 69

Epic 1 — Question Answering 
US-102 — As a student, I want one question to search multiple documents, so that I can understand a topic 
covered across several sources. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
Retrieval is performed across the full corpus. 
●​
Relevant chunks may come from multiple documents. 
●​
The final response identifies the supporting sources. 
Epic 2 — Citations 
US-201 — As an assignment writer, I want every answer to include a citation, so that I can verify the information. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
At least one real source is shown for a supported answer. 
●​
Citation includes document title and page/section when available. 
●​
Citation metadata matches the indexed source. 
Epic 2 — Citations 
US-202 — As a student, I want to inspect the source chunk, so that I can understand the context behind the 
answer. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
Citation can be expanded when the feature is implemented. 
●​
The displayed chunk is the actual retrieved text. 
●​
Source metadata is visible. 
Epic 3 — Safe Refusal 
US-301 — As a student, I want the system to say it does not know when the library does not cover my question, 
so that I do not mistake an unsupported answer for a reliable one. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
An out-of-corpus test question triggers the refusal path. 
●​
No unsupported factual answer is generated. 
●​
The response clearly states that the available materials do not support an answer. 
Epic 4 — Filtering 
US-401 — As a student, I want to limit search to a course or document type, so that I can focus on relevant 
materials. 
Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
User can select a supported filter. 
●​
Retrieval respects the selected scope. 
●​
The filter is optional and does not prevent corpus-wide search. 
Epic 5 — Session 
US-501 — As a student, I want to see previous questions and answers during my session, so that I can continue 
my research conversation. 
University Library Research Assistant — PRD v1.0.0 | Team 05 | Squad 69

Acceptance Criteria: 
●​
Current-session messages remain visible. 
●​
History is not required to persist across separate sessions.

14. Acceptance Criteria 
AC-1 — Corpus & Ingestion 
●​
Assigned corpus is inventoried for document count, formats, length, and extraction quality. 
●​
At least 5–10 representative documents are manually inspected before full indexing. 
●​
Documents are cleaned and chunked using the agreed strategy. 
●​
Each indexed chunk contains the required source metadata. 
AC-2 — Retrieval 
●​
A user question retrieves top-k relevant chunks from across the indexed corpus. 
●​
The retrieval result contains document metadata and page/section information where available. 
●​
The correct supporting chunk appears in top-k for at least 80% of the ground-truth questions (target). 
AC-3 — Answer Generation 
●​
Supported questions produce concise answers based only on retrieved content. 
●​
The system does not intentionally use unsupported external facts. 
●​
Answers meet the agreed target of at least 80% accuracy on the ground-truth evaluation set. 
AC-4 — Citations 
●​
Every supported answer displays at least one citation. 
●​
Each citation identifies the source document and page/section when available. 
●​
Citation details correspond to actual indexed metadata and are not fabricated by the LLM. 
AC-5 — Refusal Path 
●​
Out-of-corpus questions in the evaluation set trigger an explicit refusal. 
●​
The refusal clearly communicates that the answer is not covered by the available materials. 
●​
The system does not guess when no chunk meets the configured relevance threshold. 
AC-6 — UI & Performance 
●​
Chat interface accepts and displays questions and answers clearly. 
●​
Citations are visually distinguishable from the main answer. 
●​
Source chunks can be expanded if FR-17 is implemented. 
●​
End-to-end query response targets approximately 8–10 seconds or less for the live demo. 
AC-7 — Documentation & Viva Readiness 
●​
Architecture and major pipeline decisions are documented. 
●​
The team can explain ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, thresholding, generation, and citation flow. 
University Library Research Assistant — PRD v1.0.0 | Team 05 | Squad 69

●​
The evaluation set is version-controlled and rerun after major pipeline changes. 
Appendix A — Glossary 
Term 
Definition 
RAG 
Retrieval-Augmented Generation — a workflow that 
retrieves source content before generating an answer. 
Corpus 
The assigned collection of library documents used by 
the assistant. 
Chunk 
A smaller piece of a document stored and retrieved 
independently. 
Embedding 
A numerical vector representation used to compare 
semantic similarity. 
Vector Database 
A database optimized for storing and searching vector 
representations. 
Top-k Retrieval 
Returning the k highest-ranked chunks for a query. 
Relevance Threshold 
Minimum similarity/relevance level required before the 
system may answer. 
Grounded Answer 
An answer supported by the retrieved corpus content. 
Citation 
Traceable source information identifying the document 
and page/section supporting an answer. 
Refusal 
An explicit response that the available corpus does 
not contain enough information to answer. 
OCR 
Optical Character Recognition used to extract text 
from scanned documents.
